claims.statement: TermindApp shares its AppModel and persistence container across main WindowGroup scenes; if diagnosis consent is needed the scene displays DiagnosisConsentView instead of creating RootView, otherwise ordinary/restored scenes construct a fresh WindowModel (or use the demo-configured model for a debug screenshot launch without a request ID). RootView holds the model in @State and provides it to the environment and focused scene commands; the separate external-authentication Window is excluded from ordinary scene-opening commands.

RootView retains its window model while app/native registries discover windows weakly. Native close preserves prior vetoes and saves theme edits, prompting only for remaining unsaved changes even in empty windows, never merely for live connections. Discard approves only the second alert button. Quit flushes all windows' themes, protects remaining unsaved edits, then checks SFTP pending uploads before bounded shutdown, without live-workspace confirmation.

WindowModel separates destination, sidebar mode, page selections/searches, presentation routes and focused workspace state; user sidebar activation can restore Assistant's prior destination, while History is disallowed for focused Telnet/serial sessions.

The persistent workspace deck retains all open workspace views, gates hidden interaction/accessibility, parks hidden layouts at identity-keyed cached usable sizes, and prunes closed IDs rather than relaying every container resize to hidden split trees.

WorkspaceContentView renders stable-ID split leaves and fraction-based branches, previews divider movement locally, keeps a dragged source mounted while omitting it from preview geometry, and disables hidden-workspace shortcut owners.

Vault list and detail children retain identity across the split breakpoint; a covered list keeps its cached size, and detail transitions animate position and reserved space rather than resizing the form.

ManagedCardPage supplies typed sections, stable item IDs, externally owned selection, capabilities and business views to a reusable renderer; drop geometry yields stable-ID mutation intent while resource-specific actions and presentation remain with the page. Selection updates intersect section item IDs, single-selection mode uses section order, and selected-card actions receive ordered selected items. CardPage uses native blank-canvas hit testing and reference-held geometry; blank clicks clear selection before feature primary actions. Reordering filters section capabilities and policy and excludes moving IDs before sibling resolution; collapsed sections append. Hosts disables reordering during query/tag filtering; Known Hosts supplies no reorder capability. Deletion presentation delegates mutation and pruning to features; Hosts owns group delete versus keep-host choices. Hosts also owns inline review top content and captures eligibility on entry using AppReviewInvitationVisit, rather than a global RootView presenter. Shared device-local AppReviewController requires seven days, a host, enabled operation and no response; filtering or losing hosts hides without consumption, responses hide across windows, and rejected URL opens do not consume the invitation. Managed top content remains available with empty/no-results states and is excluded from blank-canvas and reorder targeting.

The workspace compact Assistant shares a window-local Chat/Archive route with full Assistant but its contextual panel opens conversations without replacing the foreground workspace; transcript and interaction regions receive explicit focused-terminal context, and Escape does not close a conversation when a blocking interaction is present.

TFM transcript owners are cached per window by conversation and surface, preserving native list and presentation state across mounts; the default eight-owner LRU trims unmounted candidates without forcibly evicting mounted surfaces.

ResponsivePageLayoutTests includes visible-window-gated narrow editor cases in English and both Chinese variants, while its offscreen Metrics case verifies native table identity, sorting and scroll retention across width changes.

TFM Welcome projects only this installation's recent connection events and uses their local timestamps, while the History sidebar searches the synchronized all-device timeline and caps displayed matches at 100.

Saved-host SSH-family terminals (SSH, Mosh and Eternal Terminal), Telnet and SFTP panes own connection-history events; closing ends the event, moving preserves it, and Serial or unsaved targets are excluded.

TFM History rows resolve each event's sourceDeviceID through the reusable app-wide device directory, so the displayed device name follows directory updates rather than remaining a hostname captured inside the event.

On macOS 26+ the native NavigationSplitView owns the Sidebar background with no extra glass overlay; older systems use an AppKit visual-effect fallback. The mode rail uses one glass capsule with a neutral moving highlight, selected accessibility traits, a key-window focus outline and Reduce Motion-aware animation.

Compact and full Assistant share conversation and Archive state; contextual actions preserve workspace navigation, full navigation replaces it, and closing the last workspace promotes selected Chat or Archive only in Assistant sidebar mode.

MainWindowCoordinator requests a UUID-valued main scene for workspace moves, retaining source ownership until native destination registration; extraction transfers the live workspace without disconnecting or recording close history, with no persistent-close authorization to cancel.

Registered native window dismissal removes source requests, unregisters the model and calls idempotent closeForWindow, recording recovery before disconnect and clearing window state while preserving managed attachments without queueing remote termination. Restored scenes retain their system-restored frames.

The Navigator's workspace inline rename starts with the full localized displayed title before the native field receives focus; commits delegate to WindowModel, which rejects unrenameable workspaces, trims names and stores split-workspace names on the group but single-pane names on the pane.

The Navigator overlays an AppKit-compatible workspace layout drop receiver above native List rows; it uses live window drag state and measured row frames to preview insertion, excluding the dragged workspace when calculating its mutation index, then reorders a workspace or detaches a pane only on a valid drop in Navigator mode.

Workspace row drag state starts on macOS 26 only after the native List drag session becomes active, while older systems set it in onDrag; the model documents that an older release outside a destination can leave stale drag state until the next click/drag, so drop callbacks validate the pasteboard.

Workspace Navigator expansion is a persisted presentation preference, independently of workspace ownership: selecting a Vault or workspace destination expands its section, and its row menu routes selection-sensitive pane actions through the window model.

The Snippets sidebar filters shared host-library snippets with a sidebar-local footer and can insert into a live focused SSH/Telnet terminal; executing a risk-classified snippet requires an additional confirmation. Its persisted package-folding state is distinct from the full Snippets page's expansion.

The History sidebar projects session-owned memory-only SSH command history, session-owned memory-only SFTP browse history, or connection history according to the selected workspace's focused pane, while Snippets and History use AppKit ListViewKit-backed rows with separate footer search and blank-area menus rather than changing the titlebar Find target.
Toolbar creation actions derive from the foreground destination rather than the sidebar mode, while Vault Navigator row menus reuse per-page creation verbs even when that page is not in front.

Find follows foreground destination and focused pane, binding retained Vault, Assistant, Metrics, built-in-theme scheme and custom-theme-library queries or focused SSH/Serial/SFTP queries. Welcome owns content search; other Settings routes and empty panes have none. Telnet reports terminal Find and presents it but lacks a toolbar query binding.

Find commands target the focused window model, which suppresses pane keyboard claims before activating terminal search and focusing the toolbar control; Welcome redirects focus into its content field and unsearchable destinations do nothing. Toolbar focus ownership is released on explicit user exit so panes may reclaim the keyboard.

On macOS 26+ a background search host contributes system searchable UI without rebuilding the persistent split-view branch; earlier macOS uses an explicit toolbar search field or compact Metrics popover, retaining native field identity and reserving toolbar height even when no Find is offered.

A focused Telnet session resolves to terminal Find and can present search from the command, but the current toolbar findContext terminal branch only binds Serial and SSH sessions, so Telnet has no usable titlebar query binding through that path.

Navigator drop positions within the List receiver clamp to Workspace insertion boundaries rather than requiring the pointer to be inside an individual Workspace row; insertion mutation excludes the dragged workspace.

Workspace tear-off extends the existing List source on macOS 26 and later, configuring failed-drop animation at native willBegin and requesting a new window only for an unaccepted, uncancelled release outside the source frame; Pane titles use a separate native completion source.
Pane moves wait for native destination registration; split panes retain the live Pane in a new Workspace while lone panes retain their original Workspace and name.

The main scene's fresh ordinary WindowModel starts at Vault/Welcome; registration injects shared connections, host and metrics models, connection-history tracking and a shared conversation store while each window retains its own workspace and query state.
The main WindowGroup suppresses automatic XCTest windows by default in debug unless TERMIND_WINDOW_TESTS=1, and disables main-scene restoration for tests and screenshot demo launches.

RootView binds native split-view visibility to window sidebar state and keeps every workspace mounted in a detail deck, activating displayedWorkspace and layering the selected non-workspace destination above it; the floating status bar appears only over a selected workspace.
A persistent root-owned window activity bridge reports key-window activation to onboarding independently of transient pane rendering; WindowTitleCatalog supplies the root navigation title separately.

Settings routes are window-local; Back climbs parents before restoring the previous destination, falling back to Vault for a removed workspace. Leaving custom-theme editing attempts autosave; invalid, deleted or failed-save drafts block navigation pending discard/cancel, while successful saves clear the editor. Discard cannot resurrect deleted themes.

SettingsPageView applies draft cleanup on route changes and disappearance: incomplete providers and new MCP servers may be discarded, while a new skill with substantive content can be retained as an inert unnamed draft rather than discarded simply for lacking a name.

WindowModel owns the Vault page and optional work route; opening a page clears the editor route, opening a work route selects its page, and closing work dismisses the route, while VaultWorkDetailView selects a route-keyed resource-specific detail.

VaultWorkEditingSession guards dirty editor transitions with tokened registrations and busy/commit fencing: navigation offers save, discard or cancel, explicit cancellation offers keep editing or discard, and only a successful async save executes its deferred transition. Failed saves leave the editor open; stale editors cannot unregister replacements.

DeviceDirectoryModel invalidates cached names after successful local rename or sync-triggered reload, and reports repository failures through storageError: failed loads yield no directory records, failed renames do not change the current name, and connection-history rows display a dash if the directory cannot resolve an event's device ID.

When the selected combinable workspace is being dragged, WindowModel derives displayedWorkspace as an eligible adjacent merge target without changing selectedWorkspace; RootView activates that deck child and Navigator highlights it, while clearing the drag restores the selected view and no eligible neighbour leaves it displayed.

If scene creation is unavailable a workspace move request does not remove the source workspace; closing the source before destination registration cancels its requests and disconnects its sessions so the late target cannot take a live workspace from it.

On macOS 26+ the background host supplies system searchable UI for findKind except theme libraries, which keep a visible native field on every OS; custom-theme editors instead supply import/delete controls. Host query and callbacks use findContext and dismissal releases keyboard ownership; Telnet lacks a binding and therefore reads empty and ignores edits.

WindowModel prevents direct selection of History when the focused pane is Telnet or Serial and reconciles an already-invalid History mode to Snippets; user mode activation also restores the previous destination on returning to Navigator from full Assistant, falling back to Vault if its workspace has closed.

MainWindowCoordinator records ordinary-size and sidebar-width fallback from registered main windows, prioritizing the most recently used window; requested scenes inherit source layout, but restored scenes retain their system frame, and requested full-screen waits for the new window to become key.
Main-window registration disallows AppKit tabbing; sizing converts between native content and frame dimensions without imposing custom titlebar geometry.

MainWindowSizeStore validates device-local persisted content size and sidebar width, defaulting to a 1180×740 main size, 320-point visible sidebar when unset; these fallback dimensions do not override individual restored scene frames.

Main-window sizing uses ordinary content coordinates: full-screen requests inherit the source's pre-full-screen size, resize tracking excludes transitions, and the destination enters full-screen only once key; requested frames honor minimum content size and are fitted to the selected screen.

The sidebar width handshake protects a requested width from the split view's initial default measurement; the preferred width changes only after an expected native measurement, and hiding the sidebar preserves its last valid width.

DesignTokens centralizes fixed layout metrics and system-adaptive semantic colors, material/glass and motion modifiers: the sidebar range is 260–520 points with a protected 360-point detail minimum, and sidebar rows draw key/inactive selection styling rather than relying on List selection colors.
The coordinator coalesces repeated requests to move the same workspace or pane from the same source into one pending scene request until destination registration consumes it.
Welcome recent-host rows construct a native context menu per click instead of a live SwiftUI menu, preventing greeting updates from resizing its popup; a presented menu draws a row outline.
The desktop status bar is controlled by an app-wide default-enabled preference; hiding it removes workspace overlay clearance and the status-path onboarding target.
Transfers has independent open/key state and close routing; when it is key, Close Window closes Transfers and Close Workspace cannot close a workspace using stale focus.

Companion dispatch resolves the source by session ID, requiring a live SSH or connected SFTP session with directory and saved host, and focuses it for current-workspace placement. SSH ticket confirmation additionally rechecks workspace, path and ticket currency before opening SFTP; stale or failed results open nothing.

Explicit workspace, pane, others and all close paths enqueue eligible managed-session cleanup and remove local targets immediately without confirmation or awaiting termination. Application-termination closeAll bypasses new managed termination requests.

AppModel injects its app-owned RemoteSessionCloseCoordinator into windows. WindowModel builds validated managed-session requests, prioritizes requests carrying transferred SSH connections, and marks accepted sessions closing so recovery records and copyForReconnect omit the scheduled remote identity; absence of a cleanup owner or valid request preserves the reference.

RemoteSessionCloseCoordinator owns one-shot asynchronous cleanup independently of workspace lifetime, deduplicates pending remote identities and releases transferred connections exactly once. Its default 30-second deadline cancels the operation; failure or cancellation is swallowed without retry and does not undo local close or restore its suppressed recovery identity.

App-owned recently closed history keeps descriptors and in-process workspace instances, persists only records whose items all have layouts, and consumes requested items only after a destination exists and all can restore. Window records reopen in a new scene and restore selected workspace; external temporary SSH workspaces lack durable layouts.

Closing a split pane records a wrapper containing only the removed pane. Reopening retains pane identity but replaces the torn-down SSH model with copyForReconnect, unlike a live move which retains the original session.
